questions.sec: Classification and Central vs Peripheral Ladder
questions.q: The preferred antitussive class in the book's ladder is:
questions.exp: Central acting is preferred; peripheral acting is used only if there is no response (Book p259)

questions.sec: Classification and Central vs Peripheral Ladder
questions.q: Peripheral acting antitussives are used only when central acting drugs show ____.
questions.exp: Central acting (preferred) → no response → peripheral acting (Book p259)

questions.sec: Classification and Central vs Peripheral Ladder
questions.q: Central antitussives as a class are indicated for:
questions.exp: Central antitussives — use: dry cough (Book p259)

questions.q: Dextromethorphan works by inhibiting ____ receptors.
questions.exp: MOA: inhibit NMDA receptors (Book p259)

questions.q: Dextromethorphan's side-effect profile includes:
opts: Miosis with pinpoint pupils and apnea
questions.exp: S/E: abuse potential (+) (α opioids); agitation/hallucination (Book p259)

questions.q: Dextromethorphan is used for ____ cough.
questions.exp: Use: mild cough (Book p259)

questions.q: Noscapine is the central non-opioid preferred for ____ cough.
questions.exp: Noscapine — use: spasmodic cough (Book p259)

questions.q: Levopropoxyphene is used for ____ cough.
questions.exp: Levopropoxyphene — use: mild cough (Book p259)

questions.q: Which central non-opioid is matched to spasmodic cough?
questions.exp: Noscapine: spasmodic cough; dextromethorphan & levopropoxyphene: mild cough (Book p259)

questions.q: Match the opioid antitussive to its book fact.
questions.exp: Codeine → max abuse potential; Ethylmorphine → least S/E; Morphine & methadone → severe cough; class → constipation, abuse potential (+) (Book p259)

questions.q: Among mild–moderate opioid antitussives, the one with maximum abuse potential is ____.
questions.exp: Mild–moderate: codeine (max abuse potential), pholcodine, ethylmorphine (Book p259)

questions.q: The mild–moderate opioid antitussive with the least S/E is ____.
questions.exp: Ethylmorphine: least S/E (Book p259)

questions.q: The opioids the book lists for severe cough are:
questions.exp: Severe: morphine, methadone (Book p259)

questions.q: Opioid antitussives cause constipation and carry a (+) ____.
questions.exp: S/E: constipation; abuse potential (+) (Book p259)

questions.q: Match the miscellaneous central antitussive to its MOA/use.
questions.exp: Diphenhydramine → H1(-)/muscarinic(-), mild cough; Aprepitant → NK1(-), severe cough; Gabapentin/pregabalin → chronic idiopathic cough (Book p259)

questions.q: Aprepitant suppresses cough by blocking ____ receptors.
questions.exp: MOA: neurokinin 1 (-); use: severe cough (Book p259)

questions.q: Chronic idiopathic cough is treated with:
questions.exp: Gabapentin/pregabalin: chronic idiopathic cough (Book p259)

questions.q: As an antitussive, diphenhydramine acts by:
questions.exp: MOA: H1(-)/muscarinic(-); use: mild cough (Book p259)

questions.q: Peripheral antitussives act on the:
questions.exp: Peripheral antitussives act on lung (Book p259)

questions.q: Match the peripheral antitussive to its mechanism.
right: Open K+ channels in peripheral nerves → (-) action potential for cough reflex
Persistent depolarisation → (-) cough impulse reaching brain
questions.exp: Local anesthetics → (-) stretch receptors; Moguisteine → open K+ channels, (-) AP for cough reflex; Cromolyn → persistent depolarisation, (-) cough impulse to brain (Book p259)

questions.q: Moguisteine opens ____ channels in peripheral nerves, suppressing the action potential of the cough reflex.
questions.exp: Open K+ channels in peripheral nerves → (-) action potential for cough reflex (Book p259)

questions.q: Cromolyn causes persistent ____, blocking the cough impulse from reaching the brain.
questions.exp: Persistent depolarisation → (-) cough impulse reaching brain (Book p259)

questions.q: Which trio of local anesthetics is listed under peripheral antitussives?
questions.exp: Drugs: lidocaine, bupivacaine, mexiletine (Book p259)

questions.q: Expectorants work via gastric irritation → reflex ____ irritation → bronchial contraction → clearance of secretions.
questions.exp: Gastric irritation → reflex bronchial irritation → bronchial contraction → clearance of secretion (Book p260)

questions.q: The only FDA-approved expectorant is ____.
questions.exp: Guaifenesin: only FDA approved drug (Book p260)

questions.q: Guaifenesin is used as:
questions.exp: Use: expectorant + antitussive (Book p260)

questions.q: The non–FDA-approved expectorants listed are:
questions.exp: Other expectorants: iodides, hypertonic saline — non-FDA approved (Book p260)

questions.q: Mucolytics break down and ____ mucus to facilitate its removal.
questions.exp: MOA: break down & liquify mucus → facilitate removal (Book p260)

questions.q: Match the mucolytic mechanism to its drugs.
questions.exp: Sulphydryl → N-acetyl/methyl/ethyl cysteine; ↑sialomucin → carbocisteine, letosteine, erdosteine, stepronin; depolymerise → bromhexine, ambroxol; DNase → cystic fibrosis (Book p260)

questions.q: Which mucolytic breaks disulphide bonds via sulphydryl groups?
questions.exp: Sulphydryl groups break disulphide bonds: N-acetylcysteine, methyl cysteine, ethyl cysteine (Book p260)

questions.q: Drugs that liquify mucus by increasing sialomucin production are:
questions.exp: ↑ sialomucin production → liquifies mucus: carbocisteine, letosteine, erdosteine, stepronin (Book p260)

questions.q: The mucolytics that depolymerise mucopolysaccharides are bromhexine and ____.
questions.exp: Depolymerise mucopolysaccharides: bromhexine, ambroxol (Book p260)

questions.q: Thick secretions of cystic fibrosis are broken by ____.
questions.exp: DNase: break thick secretions in cystic fibrosis (Book p260)

questions.q: Cough syrup for productive cough = expectorant + mucolytic + bronchodilator (____) + nasal decongestant (phenylephrine).
questions.exp: Expectorant + mucolytic + bronchodilator (salbutamol) + nasal decongestant (phenylephrine) (Book p260)

questions.q: The nasal decongestant component of the productive-cough syrup is:
questions.exp: Nasal decongestant (phenylephrine) (Book p260)

units.title: Classification and Central vs Peripheral Ladder
units.sec: Classification and Central vs Peripheral Ladder · p259
units.guide: Antitussives: central acting (preferred) → if no response → peripheral acting. Central antitussives are used for dry cough.

units.title: Central Non-Opioid Antitussives
units.guide: Dextromethorphan: inhibit NMDA receptors; S/E abuse potential (+) (α opioids), agitation/hallucination; mild cough. Noscapine: spasmodic cough. Levopropoxyphene: mild cough.

units.title: Central Opioid Antitussives
units.guide: Mild–moderate: codeine (max abuse potential), pholcodine, ethylmorphine (least S/E). Severe: morphine, methadone. Class S/E: constipation; abuse potential (+).

units.title: Miscellaneous Central Drugs
units.guide: Diphenhydramine: H1(-)/muscarinic(-), mild cough. Aprepitant: neurokinin-1(-), severe cough. Gabapentin/pregabalin: chronic idiopathic cough.

units.title: Peripheral Antitussives
units.guide: Act on lung. Local anesthetics (lidocaine, bupivacaine, mexiletine): (-) stretch receptors. Moguisteine: open K+ channels in peripheral nerves → (-) AP for cough reflex. Cromolyn: persistent depolarisation → (-) cough impulse reaching brain.

units.title: Expectorants
units.guide: MOA: gastric irritation → reflex bronchial irritation → bronchial contraction → clearance of secretion. Guaifenesin: only FDA approved, use expectorant + antitussive. Iodides & hypertonic saline: non-FDA approved.

units.title: Mucolytics
units.guide: Break down & liquify mucus → facilitate removal. Sulphydryl break disulphide bonds: N-acetyl/methyl/ethyl cysteine. ↑Sialomucin: carbocisteine, letosteine, erdosteine, stepronin. Depolymerise mucopolysaccharides: bromhexine, ambroxol. DNase: cystic fibrosis.

units.title: Productive Cough Syrup Composition
units.guide: Productive-cough syrup: expectorant + mucolytic + bronchodilator (salbutamol) + nasal decongestant (phenylephrine).
